# Nearest compatible objects as label donors

Retain the Met object-ID hash split and the earlier artificial-masking endpoint. Each training row has its own fold withheld from its donor table. All development rows use the training donor table. Skip reserved rows before parsing any fields beyond object ID. Add descriptive fields for medium, culture, artist nationality and the first artist's begin and end years. Also give every new fitted comparator the lexical position of the full accession string among training strings. Object ID is available to all models.

Test the hypothesis that inventory neighbours within a narrow acquisition range transfer a recorded declaration more reliably when their descriptive fields are compatible. For each record, retrieve up to eight preceding and eight following training records in each of inventory-ID order and accession-string order. Weight each neighbour by inverse square-root rank offset and a product of fixed bonuses for matching nonempty artist, family, department, classification, name, medium, and similar object dates. Use smoothed class rates, effective counts and closest matching-neighbour rates as features of a supervised predictor. The accession tie-breaker is object ID. Include the matching model with only global-ID windows, the unweighted two-order window model, and a richer metadata-only classifier. Use the same GPU CatBoost configuration and the same predictors apart from the tested donor information. Include the direct compatible rate, the CPU original neighbour model and preceding GPU global-ID model in the gate. A development screen requires .005 nats lower pooled mean log loss than every comparator. No test labels are opened. A gain would merit independent investigation on real metadata-repair workloads.
